sunrise.options.server_stick.tooltip: How the stick moves on a server. Java moves only by its keys, so a server's anticheat may pull you back for the stick's own speed and angle. Analog: as you push it (servers that do not check). Free Direction: any angle at full speed, by turning the look the server sees (others see your head follow; it turns back to your view for every hit, use and block). D-pad: arrows on screen in the stick's place (a controller's stick takes the nearest of their eight directions), at full speed. A server you picked a mode for when it pulled you back keeps that one; change this while playing there to change it.
sunrise.options.stick_prompt.tooltip: When a server keeps pulling you back while the stick moves you, ask how the stick should move there.
starling.stick_prompt.title: This Server Pulls You Back
starling.stick_prompt.body: Its anticheat (Grim or one like it) takes only the moves Java's keys make, and the stick's own speed and angle are not one of them. Pick how the stick moves here; Options > Controls > Controller Settings changes it any time.
Sets distance, particles, shadows, sky a: Sets distance, particles, shadows, sky and fog; changing one makes it Custom.

starling.perf.title: Performance test (test builds only)
starling.perf.about: Tap Start and keep playing normally: every 30 seconds Starling switches how the world is drawn, and at the end it tells you what runs fastest on your phone. Menus, pauses and idle time don't count.
starling.perf.waiting: This setup: play a little to see its average.
starling.perf.share: Test builds send these results to Starling's developers on their own; the diagnostic ZIP has them too.
starling.perf.guided.running: Performance test %s/%s · keep playing normally · %s left
starling.perf.guided.intro: This test build checks what runs fastest on your phone: keep playing normally for a few minutes while it switches how the world is drawn every 30 seconds. The results (GPU, settings and FPS, nothing personal) go to Starling's developers. You can stop it in Options → Diagnostics.
starling.perf.guided.done: Performance test done: the fastest here is %s (%s fps, against %s with Auto). Options → Diagnostics → Use the fastest switches to it.
starling.perf.guided.done_auto: Performance test done: Auto is already the fastest here (%s fps). Thank you!
starling.perf.guided.sent: The results are on their way to Starling's developers. Thank you!
starling.calibrate.title: Calibrate Performance
starling.calibrate.about: Starling opens a test world for a minute or two and tries each way of drawing that shows the very same picture (how terrain is drawn, when the sky is drawn, culling), then keeps the fastest. Distance, resolution and shadows stay as they are. Nothing leaves your phone.
starling.calibrate.later: Calibration runs once the game has started.
starling.calibrate.never: Not calibrated yet: Starling draws the way it expects to be fastest on this GPU (Auto).
starling.calibrate.done: Calibrated in %s: the fastest here is %s (%s fps, against %s fps with Auto). It is in use now.
starling.calibrate.done_auto: Calibrated in %s: Auto is already the fastest here (%s fps).
starling.calibrate.stopped_by_you: Calibration stopped: it needs the game in front with no menu open. Nothing changed.
starling.calibrate.wait_loading: Wait for the game to finish loading to calibrate.
starling.calibrate.leave_world: Leave the world for the title screen to calibrate.
starling.calibrate.running: Calibrating %s/%s · about %s left · don't touch the screen · Back stops it
